paragraphs.source_en: Chaya Shirōjirō left before Ogin. At the gate, he involuntarily halted and stood there dazed for a long while. paragraphs.source_en: According to Ishida Mitsunari, Hideyoshi would return to Osaka around the thirteenth or fourteenth of the seventh month. By now he should have reached Bizen Okayama; therefore, the imperial envoy being sent to welcome him should also depart Kyoto within the next day or two. That being so, Ieyasu too would have to enter the capital and offer congratulations upon the Kanpaku’s triumphal return. But if an unexpected stroke were made at that moment, it would truly be a bolt from the blue, catching them wholly unprepared!
